description:
## Background

bsm-nd7.3 made each Child Issue entry in Issue Detail a keyboard-operable button. Activating a button updates Issue Detail to the child Issue and removes the parent's Child Issues section (the section that contained the activated button) from the DOM. Because the activated button is unmounted in the same render, the browser cannot keep focus on it; focus falls back to `<body>`. Screen reader and keyboard users lose their place after every Child Issue navigation, and the new Issue's content is not announced.

## Goal

After activating a Child Issue button (mouse click, Enter, or Space), move focus to a sensible location inside the new Issue Detail so keyboard users can continue navigating and assistive technology announces the change. The behavior must distinguish user-driven selection changes from other reasons the selection changes:

- focus must move on activation of a Child Issue button (mouse or keyboard);
- focus must NOT move on initial mount of `IssueExplorer`;
- focus must NOT move on a workspace transition (the App-level `workspaceKey` remount drops the local `selectedIssueId` and remounts the explorer; focus management should not fire in that case);
- focus management for Child Issue activation must not change the existing `handleSelect` signature, the Child Issue button's DOM contract, or the Issue List's `aria-current` row indicator.

## What to build

- Add a user-driven selection change mechanism that the Child Issue button's `onClick` and `onKeyDown` handlers set before calling `handleSelect`, and that the focus-management effect reads and clears.
- Move focus to the Issue Detail's title heading (`<h2>` inside `IssueDetailContent`) using a `ref` callback. Use `focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the existing layout is not disturbed.
- Add `aria-live="polite"` on the detail pane's `<main>` element so the new Issue's content is announced when the selection changes, even when focus is moved elsewhere.

## Technical Approach

- Introduce a `useRef`-backed flag in `IssueExplorer` that records whether the next `selectedIssueId` change is user-driven. `ChildIssueRow`'s button `onClick` and `onKeyDown` handlers (Enter and Space, both of which natively activate a button) set this flag before calling `handleSelect`. Issue List row clicks do not set the flag; the `aria-current` row indicator behavior continues to be driven by the visible list.
- Add a `useEffect` keyed on `selectedIssueId` that, when the flag is set, focuses the detail heading through a `ref` on `<h2>` and then clears the flag. The effect does not move focus when the flag is not set, so initial mount, workspace transitions, and non-Child-Issue selection changes are no-ops.
- The flag is reset to `false` at the end of the effect, so a later non-user selection change does not move focus.
- Add `aria-live="polite"` (or `role="status"`) to the detail pane's `<main>` element. `IssueDetailEmpty` is the empty-state branch and does not need the live region; only the populated `IssueDetailContent` receives it.
- The plan must not introduce a focus-management library, a global focus trap, or a programmatic scroll. The detail is already visible; the user did not request scrolling.

## Considerations

- The flag is local to the explorer's React subtree. It is reset by the App-level `workspaceKey` remount, so workspace transitions cannot leave the flag set across a remount.
- Mouse click on a Child Issue button must also set the flag. The activation must be a single `onClick` handler that sets the flag and calls `onSelect(issue.id)`. The `onKeyDown` handler must intercept only Enter and Space and set the flag before calling `onSelect`.
- The plan must not change `handleSelect`, the `IssueExplorer` `useState` shape, or the `ChildIssueRow` `onSelect` prop type.
- The plan must not affect the existing `aria-current` row indicator on the Issue List, the cross-view Child Issue navigation tests, the selection-persistence tests, or the removal/workspace-transition tests.
- Keyboard activation tests in the `Child Issue navigation` describe block must continue to pass without modification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clicking a Child Issue button moves focus to the Issue Detail's title heading.
- [ ] Pressing Enter on a focused Child Issue button moves focus to the Issue Detail's title heading.
- [ ] Pressing Space on a focused Child Issue button moves focus to the Issue Detail's title heading.
- [ ] Focus is NOT moved on initial mount of `IssueExplorer`.
- [ ] Focus is NOT moved after a workspace transition (React `key` change on the explorer's parent).
- [ ] Focus is NOT moved when an Issue List row is clicked (or any non-Child-Issue selection change).
- [ ] The Issue Detail's `<main>` has an `aria-live="polite"` attribute (or equivalent) that announces the new Issue's content.
- [ ] The Issue List's `aria-current` row indicator continues to track the visible selected row, and the existing `selection persistence` and `removal and workspace transition clearing` tests still pass.

## Test Plan

- Extend the focused component tests in `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`:
  - assert `document.activeElement` is the detail heading after a mouse click on a Child Issue button;
  - assert `document.activeElement` is the detail heading after Enter on a focused Child Issue button;
  - assert `document.activeElement` is the detail heading after Space on a focused Child Issue button;
  - assert `document.activeElement` is NOT the detail heading on initial mount;
  - assert `document.activeElement` is NOT the detail heading after a React `key` change on the explorer's parent.
- Add a screen-reader announcement assertion: the detail `<main>` element has the expected `aria-live` attribute, and after a Child Issue activation, the new Issue's title is discoverable as the live region's text.
- Run `pnpm test`, Ultracite checks, and the TypeScript / Vite build for `src/issues/`.

## Non-goals and follow-up boundaries

- Do not change Child Issue ordering, empty-state visibility, selection-clearing behavior, or the `handleSelect` signature (these are owned by bsm-nd7.1 through bsm-nd7.3).
- Do not add a focus-management library, a global focus trap, or a focus ring utility.
- Do not extend the real-desktop WebDriver E2E coverage (bsm-nd7.4) to test focus management; the focused component tests above are the right surface for this UX detail.
- Do not move focus when an Issue List row is clicked or when the selection changes for a non-Child-Issue reason.
- Do not introduce programmatic scrolling, smooth-scroll behavior, or any other layout change as a side effect.
- Do not add a second selection state or a new RPC call.
title: Manage focus after Child Issue navigation
